comparator.name: Chinese Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The live Leiden Study Guide product identifies a current 180-EC Chinese Studies bachelor with three 60-EC years and no formal graduation routes. The coherent pathway represented here combines every compulsory component with a political-economy-and-society emphasis in the restricted choices. Year 1 contains 55 EC of compulsory Mandarin, classical Chinese, Chinese history, contemporary China, Chinese culture and digital-humanities study plus the 5-EC Classics of Asia bound elective. Year 2 contains 25 EC of compulsory language, contemporary-China and philosophy-of-science study, 15 EC of selected China-focused content, one 5-EC shared East Asia course and the 15-EC Mandarin 2c study period in China or Taiwan. Year 3 contains 10 EC of compulsory Mandarin, one 5-EC Chinese-language choice, one 5-EC China-focused content choice, a 10-EC BA paper and 30 EC of genuine elective space. The selected content choices form one valid political-economy-and-society pathway; they are not a formal route and were selected independently of UCR fit. The zero-credit first-year mentoring component is noted in the official product but omitted from the positive-credit component list.

exception.reason: Leiden Chinese Studies is an integrated area-studies and language degree. Its defining core contains a cumulative modern Mandarin sequence, classical Chinese, Chinese-language source work, Chinese history and culture across premodern and modern periods, contemporary Chinese politics, economics and society, region-specific disciplinary choices, an intensive study period in China or Taiwan and an independent Chinese Studies paper. UCR offers strong general courses in history, politics, international relations, sociology, economics, literature, media, philosophy and cultural heritage, but it offers no Mandarin or classical Chinese language sequence, no Chinese-language source training, no China- or East-Asia-focused course sequence and no comparable situated study or Chinese Studies research environment. A 24-course UCR programme would therefore replace the programme's defining language-and-area formation with adjacent general disciplines rather than constitute a defensible Chinese Studies comparison.
exception.curriculumContext: The live 2026-2027 Leiden curriculum accounts for exactly 180 EC across three 60-EC years. The represented pathway preserves 55 EC of Year 1 compulsory work plus one 5-EC bound elective; 25 EC of Year 2 compulsory work, 15 EC of selected China-focused content, one 5-EC shared East Asia course and one 15-EC Mandarin 2c option; and 10 EC of compulsory third-year Mandarin, one 5-EC language option, one 5-EC content option, a 10-EC BA paper and 30 EC of open elective space. There is no formal route. The restricted choices instantiate one coherent political-economy-and-society emphasis without changing the programme's broad identity.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. GOSHIST111 Modern History, GOSHIST211 History of Empires and GOSHIST312 History Research Seminar provide historical frameworks and research practice; GOSPOLI112 Foundations of Comparative Politics, GOSPOLI212 Theory of International Relations, BENECON111 Introduction to Economics, BENECON211 International Macroeconomics, BENENTR312 International Business & Governance, GOSSOCI111 Introduction to Sociology, GOSSOCI214 Modern Sociology and GOSSOCI212 Qualitative Research Methodology support political, economic and social analysis; MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature, MCCMEDI111 Introduction to Film & Media, MCCMEDI311 Media & Race, MCCHEAM111 Introduction to Western Art History and GOSPHIL111 Introduction to Western Philosophy provide general cultural, literary, media, heritage and philosophical study. These are transferable disciplinary perspectives, not China-specific courses. The workbook contains no Mandarin course, classical Chinese, Chinese linguistics, Chinese history, Chinese literature, Chinese philosophy or religion, Chinese politics or economy, East Asian regional studies, Chinese-language primary-source training, China/Taiwan study component or Chinese Studies research capstone. It therefore cannot support an academically honest 24-course closest match.
